text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak emphasise "the need to implement peace agreements and continuing the circle of peace". The two leaders warn of a deterioration in the situation and call for a "balanced and fair accord".
- 240 million dinars ($338 million) is the estimated budget of the state-owned telecommunications company in 1997.
- Israeli ambassador Shamir opens the Israeli trade fair organised by a private sector company; a large protest staged against it with around 1,000 demonstrators participating.
- Senate debates 1997 budget for final approval.
- 325,000 citizens benefited from literacy programmes, says education minister, adding that educational system has succeeded in spreading basic education.

- In a "peaceful atmosphere and with reason prevailing", the sit-in against the Israeli exhibition attains its aim; the campaign continues with a three-day work stoppage for lawyers and an hour a day stoppage for unions.
- Supply Ministry completes its preparations for the holy Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
- Amman is designated as the headquarters of the Council of Arab Businessmen at the end of a meeting of Arab businessmen, with Cairo designated as the venue of next meeting in 1998.
- Jordan and Egypt caution Israel against troops pullout delay, say Israel should respect the accords agreed with the Palestinians.
